question.text: Per IPEV 2022 Guidelines, the Net Asset Valuation (NAV) method is MOST appropriate for valuing which type of investee company?

answer.text: A fast-growing SaaS startup with 100%+ YoY revenue growth
A listed midcap pharma with 5 years of profit history
Any company with positive EBITDA and P/E above 30
A loss-making investee in finance/investment business or one with poor performance

explanation.text: The Logic: Per PDF Section 11.8.3 point 4: 'Where the investee company is NOT performing satisfactorily and incurring losses, or it is in the BUSINESS OF FINANCE AND INVESTMENTS, it may be valued by reference to its net tangible assets.' For going-concern high-growth companies, DCF or multiples are preferred. The Trap: Fast-growing SaaS → DCF or revenue multiples; listed midcap pharma → market price; high-multiple company → relative valuation. NAV is the fallback for distress or for financial businesses where 'assets' ARE the business (banks, NBFCs, holdco). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers the same. Indian accounting standards (Ind-AS 109, 113) treat NBFC investees under fair value through OCI with NAV as a practical expedient.
